params.parameter: Blue grism: prism apex and glass
params.value: 33.90 deg in fused silica (EFFECTIVE; the true values are not published)
params.note: NOT FOUND: no document gives the grism's prism angle, glass, or blaze angle. EFFECTIVE (script model scripts in scratchpad/r11/kast/m3.js, web/physics.js read-only): the explorer's grism has its center fixed at the straight-through wavelength, lambda0 = (n - 1) sin A / G (order 1). With the glass assumed, the apex A is solved so that lambda0 equals the published 4340 A. The glass is then chosen from the published DISPERSIONS of the three blue grisms (lambda0 4780 / 4340 / 3880 A, 1.41 / 1.02 / 0.63 A/px, grooves 452 / 600 / 830): fused silica gives A = 27.78 / 33.90 / 43.08 deg and model dispersions 1.461 / 1.019 / 0.637 A/px (+3.6% / -0.1% / +1.0%); N-BK7 gives A = 24.40 / 29.62 / 37.21 deg and 1.497 / 1.062 / 0.689 (+6.2% / +4.1% / +9.4%); N-FK5, LF5, F2 and N-BAK2 fall between (+2% to +11%). Silica is the best of the six, so it is entered; INFERRED that the real glass is of low index, with an apex near 34 deg. The blue dispersion test below is therefore NOT independent (the glass was picked from it); the 452 and 830 grisms are the independent check, but are not presets.

layout.text: TR66 p. 7 (PDF p. 13), the 3-D drawing of the optical layout by Tony Misch, labeled 'Kast Double Spectrograph' (an oblique perspective with no scale bar); the Lick User's Guide redraws the same view (FIG, letter labels a-r). No plan view, ray trace or dimensioned drawing is published in any saved document. Everything below is read from this one figure, rotated upright, at 150 dpi (1650 x 1275 px; coordinates are (x, y) in that render, y down).
layout.quote: We sincerely thank Tony Misch for his superb 3-D drawing of the optical layout of the Kast spectrograph.

layout.text: The telescope beam comes down a vertical line at x = 752: decker and slit (y = 290-322), the three filter wheels (y = 330-390), the two dichroic/mirror plates #2 and #1 (y = 600-640), then the red collimator at the foot of the line (752, 925). The dichroic transmits the red straight on to the red collimator; the red collimator returns the beam up and to the right to the three gratings (y = 430-490, beside the filter wheels), and the beam goes on to the red filter turret, red camera, shutter and dewar at the right. The blue light is reflected by the dichroic up and to the left to the blue collimator at (395, 455); its returning beam runs down and to the right, past the dichroic plates, to the blue filter tray, the three grisms, the blue camera, shutter and dewar at the lower right (grisms at (1040, 790)).
layout.quote: On the red side, after striking a silvered collimator, the beam proceeds to a reflectance grating and then passes through a filter wheel

layout.text: Known dimension: the slit stands at each collimator's focus, so the slit-to-red-collimator distance is f_col = 1416 mm (SOURCED, INFERRED that the slit is at the focus). In the figure that distance runs from the slit (752, 322) to the collimator (752, 925): 603 px, so 2.35 mm/px along the vertical (the telescope axis, which an oblique projection draws near true length). Used for lengths along that axis only; horizontal and diagonal distances are foreshortened by an unknown factor.

The plates stand at y about 610: 288 px = 680 mm from the slit (48% of the way to the red collimator), then 315 px = 740 mm to the red collimator. The blue collimator is the same 1416 mm from the slit by the dichroic's reflection, so it stands 1416 - 680 = 736 mm from the dichroic (the figure draws 376 px, 880 mm, but that line is diagonal and foreshortened by an unknown amount).

The reflected blue beam leaves the plates at (735, 615) toward the blue collimator at (395, 455): a turn of about 115 deg from the downward chief ray, an angle of incidence of 32.5 deg (+-8 deg, an oblique view). No document states it. The two plates (#1 and #2) are drawn as parallel flats facing the same way.

The red collimator (752, 925) to the grating carrier (825, 478): 454 px, 1070 mm at the scale above (the beam is nearly vertical, so little foreshortening). The grating stands near the level of the filter wheels, as in LRIS, not at the pupil image of the secondary. Entered layLen = 1070 mm.

The returning red beam leaves the collimator at 10.1 deg to the incoming chief ray (lateral 80 px in 447 px of vertical travel): an off-axis paraboloid whose parent axis is tilted 5.0 deg from the incoming ray. Entered colTilt = 5.0 for both arms (the blue collimator is 'identical', TR66 p. 6; its two beam lines at the blue collimator are drawn 1.5 deg apart in the projection, too unreliable to use, so the blue value is SCHEMATIC).

The gratings (three in a tray, one used at a time, tilted by remote control) turn the beam to the camera at the right; the projected turn is about 100 deg, which is a projection artifact. The explorer's psi = 45 deg is EFFECTIVE (Parameters). The disperser-to-camera distance (camLen) is NOT drawn to scale and is left at the explorer's default.

Blue collimator, filter tray, one of three grisms (all always in place) and the camera stand in a straight line (the grism passes the straight-through wavelength undeviated): the blue camera axis lies on the collimator axis. layLen for the blue arm is entered as 1070 mm like the red (SCHEMATIC: the blue line is diagonal and the figure has no scale along it).
layout.quote: We have three grisms and they are all always in place

layout.text: OFF-AXIS (SOURCED text 'off-axis paraboloid' for both arms; the figure shows the returning beam beside, not along, the incoming one, with the slit and filter wheels outside the returning beam).

not_found: The grisms' prism apex angles, glass and blaze angles; the red gratings' blaze angles, sizes and ruled lengths (gLen): none appears in the Lick manuals, TR66, the Berkeley papers or the synopsis page. The blue apex is EFFECTIVE (fused silica, 33.90 deg).
The camera-collimator angle (psi), the gratings' angle of incidence and the grating tilt in degrees (the tilt is in motor steps with no steps-per-degree): psi = 45 deg is EFFECTIVE.
The camera lens prescriptions (elements, glass, f-ratio): only the focal length 188.7 mm, the design wavelength ranges and 'all-refractive' are published. The camera speed is DERIVED (f/2.3).
The dichroics' angle of incidence, thickness and substrate (32.5 deg is MEASURED from an oblique drawing, +-8 deg); the measured D55 curve is only an image (no data file).
The Cassegrain focal ratio and the illuminated aperture of the 3.048 m primary (secondary and baffle obstruction): F = 17.53 is DERIVED from the plate scale and the 120-inch diameter.

A measured resolving power from arc lines: only the Berkeley papers' round figures (about 6 A blue and 11 A red FWHM at 2 arcsec) and the manual's ranges (blue 700-1700, red 500-3000). The 2016 Hamamatsu upgrade has no instrument paper (only the Lick page and the BSNIP data-release notes).
A dimensioned layout, ray trace or Zemax/Code V prescription: the instrument was designed by J. S. Miller and built in the Lick shops, and the only layout published is the 3-D perspective drawing.

The system throughput as a table: the manual refers to a throughput page by J. X. Prochaska (http://www.ucolick.org/~xavier/KAST_THRU/), which is a link to a personal site that no longer serves the data; the manual's own range is 'Peak system efficiency ... between 5 and 20%' (blue, TR66 p. 8) and 'in the vicinity of 30-40%' (red, with the old detector).
conflicts: Beam size and focal ratio: UMQ and TR66 give a 82.6 mm beam on the 1416 mm collimator (F = 17.14), but the 3.86 arcsec/mm plate scale on the 3.048 m primary gives F = 17.53 and an 80.77 mm beam (and f/17.14 would need a 3.117 m pupil). The record keeps the sourced plate scale and focal length (so the pixel scale and dispersions come out as published) and takes the explorer's beam from F = 17.53. A larger secondary obstruction does not resolve it (that makes the pupil smaller, not larger). Possibly 82.6 mm is the design beam with margin.

Citation year: the Lick-posted report is dated September 1994; BSNIP I, III and the data-release paper cite 'Miller & Stone 1993'; the User's Guide is not dated. The record cites the report as posted (TR66, 1994).

Red coverage: the grating table gives 6785 A for the 300/7500 (2661 px at 2.55 A/px) but the detector page says the spectrum covers rows 760 to 3310 (2551 px, 6505 A). The record uses 2551 rows, so the model's 6489 A is 4.4% below the table. The 2016 news says the single-image coverage grew 'by about 20%' (6785 / 5520 = +23%).

D55 transition width: the manual says 'About 200 angstroms of the spectrum are affected'; the measured D55 curve (Fig. 3) has a 10-90% width of 380 A (reflectance 0.90 at 5225 A, 0.10 at 5608 A). Entered 380 A (MEASURED). The same page says the crossover is 'about 5500 A'; the curve crosses at 5450 A.

Lick's synopsis page gives the blue grism ranges as 3100-5520 A (600/4310) and 3100-6200 A (452/3306); the Quick Reference and Blue Side pages give 3300-5520 and 3150-6200 A. The record uses the User's Guide values.

Standard slit: the Lick manual's one stated default is 0.5 arcsec (arc lamps); the Berkeley supernova program's typical slit is 2 arcsec. The preset uses 2 arcsec, which also makes the published 6 A and 11 A resolutions the targets.
notes: Era and status. Kast has run since early 1992 and is in operation (the Lick pages were updated July 2025). The preset represents the current configuration: the blue Fairchild 2048 x 2048 CCD (since September 2008) and the red Hamamatsu 1024 x 4096 CCD (since 18 September 2016), both 15 um pixels. The 1994 report describes the Reticon era: two 1200 x 400 CCDs of 27 um pixels (0.78 arcsec/px, 2.35 A/px for the 600/mm gratings); its tables and tilt formulas are for that era and are not used.

Two physical spectrographs in one housing. Each arm has its own off-axis paraboloid collimator (1416 mm), its own camera (188.7 mm lens) and CCD; the dichroic sits in the diverging beam after the common slit (All-arms group 'Kast', split 'focus', slit shared, relay none). The polarimeter module (waveplate plus calcite) can replace the user filter wheels; it is not modeled.

Explorer representation. mode grating; D 3.048 m; F 17.53 (DERIVED); W 80.77 mm; fcol 1416 mm; fcam 188.7 mm; slit 2.0 arcsec; nObj 1; colTilt 5.0 deg (MEASURED from the figure; the blue value SCHEMATIC); layLen 1070 mm (red MEASURED, blue SCHEMATIC); cam lens; Nx x Ny 2048 x 2048 (blue) and 2551 x 1024 (red), pix 15 um. Blue: gType grism, G 600, gKind ruled, gGlass silica, gA 33.90 deg (EFFECTIVE), lamC 4340 A (the straight-through wavelength, fixed by the grism). Red: gType refl, G 300, lamB 7500 A, lamC 7800 A (INFERRED), psi 45 deg (EFFECTIVE).

What the explorer cannot represent: the grism's blaze (a grism of a given apex only fixes the straight-through wavelength), the moveable detector stage (blue x-stage shifts the coverage by 100-200 A), the camera's measured aberrations and flexure (up to 9 px), the dichroic's ghosts and the 10 px shift of the red spectrum, the polarimeter, and the red camera's loss of focus off the 4000-11000 A design range.
The 2016 dichroics: a new D46 (4600 A) and a D57 (5700 A) with sharper transitions and brighter ghosts are available; only the D55 (the supernova standard) is entered.
